requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is satisfied.** The implementation covers each obligation and the tests cover the main cases.

**Implementation**
- **File discovery.** `rust_files` (src/rust_coverage.rs:171) walks the project and collects every `.rs` file.
  - It skips `.git` and `target` at any depth.
  - It skips `book`, `evidence` and `vendor` only when the directory is the project root (`directory == root`).
  - Read, entry and file-type failures are pushed as errors, so a partial scan is never silent.
- **Item coverage.** `missing_function_references` (src/rust_coverage.rs:130) parses the source with the Rust outline profile.
  - The profile maps `function_item`, `function_signature_item`, `struct_item`, `enum_item` and `union_item` to outline nodes. Function signatures cover trait methods and foreign declarations (src/outline/rust.rs `KINDS`).
  - It assigns each comment to its owning node through the outline comment ownership, which the outline requirements define.
  - A comment run counts only if it holds a non-term `{impl}`, `{cite}` or `{test}` role whose name is a defined requirement or example. Unknown names and term definitions do not count.
  - The check works on parsed comment nodes, not raw text. String-literal references therefore do not count, and enclosing `mod` or `impl` comments do not count for the items inside them.
  - It reports items as `(declaration_line, kind, name)` with kinds function, struct, enum and union.
- **Reporting.** `validate_rust_functions` (src/rust_coverage.rs:225) emits `file:line: kind name has no requirement or example citation`.
  - Rust parse failures and unreadable files are reported as `cannot parse Rust source` or `cannot read Rust source`, and also added to discovery errors. They are never skipped.
  - `inspect_repository_with_progress` calls it during repository validation (src/evidence.rs:273).
- **Examples.** The requirement that a named example references a requirement is enforced in `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs), which reports an error for any example lacking a `{cite}` or `{test}` to a requirement. I judge that sufficient. Rust coverage accepts citations of any defined example, and the invalid example is still reported as a validation error.
- **Marking.** The `{impl}` markers are on the relevant functions: `inspect_repository_with_progress`, `display_name`, `missing_function_references`, `rust_files`, `validate_rust_functions` and `display_path`. I found no part of the behaviour that is implemented without an `{impl}` reference or that goes beyond the requirement.

**Tests**
- `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` checks these points:
  - enclosing `mod` and `impl` comments do not count;
  - references in strings and raw strings do not count;
  - unknown requirement names do not count;
  - body comments count;
  - a comment run followed by a blank line still attaches to the next item;
  - a trailing comment on the previous item does not leak to the next item;
  - an inner doc comment binds to its container, not the next item;
  - an outer doc comment attaches to the item it precedes.
- `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, nested functions, `{test}` on a requirement, `{test}` on a named example, and an uncited test helper.
- `locates_functions_after_unicode_text` checks line numbers after multibyte text, plus an inline block comment before a `fn` on the same line.
- `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside` covers these cases:
  - a comment attached to a struct;
  - a comment before a field or variant inside the item, which counts for the item;
  - a `{cite}` reference;
  - missing struct, enum and union reported with kind, name and line;
  - a nested struct inside a cited function reported separately.
- `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` is a filesystem test of the skip rules and error reporting.
  - It checks skipped `target` at root and nested, skipped `.git`, and skipped root-level `book`, `evidence` and `vendor`.
  - It checks that `src/vendor` and `src/book` are still scanned.
  - It checks that a broken file produces a parse-failure error and is not skipped.
- `status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form` (tests/commands.rs) and `discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference` (tests/authoring_batch.rs) check that findings and parse errors surface through the CLI and the batch author command.
- The one thing I did not see tested end to end is a Rust citation of an invalid example (one with no requirement reference), but that example is already reported as an error through the examples requirement.

No acknowledged gaps (FIXME) are present.

text: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.targets`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
